clue.text: Ultimate transformation isotope has affected

indicators.note: the words isotope and has are acted upon and changed, so their letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, as part of the letters to shuffle

explanation.surface: A physics note: some isotope has undergone the ultimate change.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has' looks like a link word but is part of the fodder; 'affected' is the anagram signal working on ISOTOPE plus HAS.
explanation.definitionFit: Deification, being raised to the status of a god, is the highest possible transformation of a being.

clue.text: Badly-drafted measures for relief?

parts.note: legislation that is badly written could be called inferior statutes; the historical English statutes governing relief of the destitute bear that very name

explanation.surface: A complaint about clumsily written welfare legislation.
explanation.walkthrough: The Poor Laws were the English statutes, from Elizabethan times to 1948, providing relief for paupers; read the other way they sound like laws of poor quality.
explanation.definitionFit: Historic English statutes organising parish relief of paupers are known by this name, which also reads as shoddy legislation.

clue.text: Dog shortly rolls over, presenting this?

definitions.text: Dog shortly rolls over, presenting this?

indicators.note: turning over, the remaining letters are read in the opposite direction
cut short, so the final letter of the dog word is dropped

parts.note: a mutt is a mongrel dog

explanation.surface: A dog rolls onto its back, offering its belly for a rub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shortly' trims MUTT to MUT, and 'rolls over' turns MUT round; the whole clue also describes what a dog shows when it rolls over.
explanation.definitionFit: A dog rolling over presents its belly, colloquially its stomach, for a rub.

clue.text: Almost executed at the wrong time

indicators.note: an executed person may be beheaded, so the head, the first letter, is removed

parts.note: almost means nearly

explanation.surface: A prisoner who was almost executed, but the timing went wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'executed' means beheaded: NEARLY loses its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Arriving before the proper or expected hour is coming untimely, premature rather than punctual.

clue.text: Drink collection full of natural flavouring

indicators.note: the collection word is filled with the flavouring, which goes inside it

parts.note: a set is a collection of things
a herb such as basil is a natural flavouring

explanation.surface: A beverage range containing natural flavours.
explanation.definitionFit: A sweet fruit-flavoured beverage, or a fizzy powder for making one; in Australia it is even slang for beer.

clue.text: One's sorry to be in this, with the Ashes coming up?

definitions.text: One's sorry to be in this, with the Ashes coming up?

parts.words: One's sorry to be in this, with the Ashes coming up
parts.note: the penitent's coarse garment goes with ashes in the phrase for showing remorse; the Ashes is also the England-Australia cricket series

explanation.surface: A cricketer regrets being caught up in something just before the Ashes series.
explanation.walkthrough: To be 'in sackcloth and ashes' is to show penitence; the Ashes is the Test series between England and Australia, giving a cricket-flavoured surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Coarse cloth worn as a sign of mourning or repentance, traditionally alongside ashes.

clue.text: Response to mistake in schedule of very idle surgeon?

definitions.meaning: an exclamation one makes on a blunder
a surgeon with nothing to do has zero operations on the list: O (nought) and OPS

explanation.walkthrough: The second reading splits the answer into O (zero) plus OPS (operations): the list of a surgeon with no work.
explanation.definitionFit: An apologetic exclamation, like whoops, is what one blurts out after a blunder.

clue.text: Thoroughly beaten, having committed bigamy to cement position of control

indicators.note: the control position is set firmly into the middle of the bigamy word

parts.note: a bigamist has married too often, so is over-wed
the helm is where a ship is steered

explanation.surface: A bigamist's attempt to strengthen his grip on power ends in utter defeat.
explanation.walkthrough: OVERWED, married too many times, is a whimsical coinage for bigamy.
explanation.definitionFit: Being completely overpowered or defeated is a synonym for being thoroughly beaten.

clue.text: Contemptible to ask too many questions about an officer

indicators.note: the prying word goes around the officer piece

parts.note: to pry is to be nosily inquisitive
the indefinite article gives A
Lt is the abbreviation for lieutenant

explanation.surface: Pestering an officer with questions is despicable.
explanation.definitionFit: Something meagre or worthless deserves scorn, so trifling and contemptible are synonyms.

clue.text: Force to accept Military Medal in trade

indicators.note: the force word takes in the medal letters

parts.note: to coerce is to force
MM is the abbreviation for the Military Medal

explanation.surface: Someone is pressured into accepting a military decoration as part of a deal.
explanation.definitionFit: Buying and selling on a large scale is a synonym for trade.

clue.text: Not on, Corleone's appalling language

indicators.note: the letters of the word on are excluded from the mix
appallingly treated, the remaining letters of the mafia name are jumbled

explanation.surface: A disapproving remark that the Godfather Corleone's language is unacceptable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not on' removes O and N from CORLEONE, and 'appalling' shuffles the remaining CRLEOE.
explanation.definitionFit: A creole is a language formed from a mix of tongues that has become native to a community.

clue.text: British and Englishman's goodness

parts.note: limey is American slang for an English person, from the limes once issued to sailors

explanation.surface: A remark on British and English virtue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'goodness' is the exclamation, as in 'my goodness!', not virtue.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are exclamations of surprise, so the British interjection swaps for 'goodness!'.

clue.text: Curse no woman would speak?

definitions.meaning: an utterance calling down evil on someone
the way of speaking used only by men

explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer as MALE DICTION: a manner of speech no woman would use.
explanation.definitionFit: A malediction is a spoken curse, the opposite of a benediction.

clue.text: Unable easily to learn way to make draw

parts.note: the word ward taken back, read the other way, spells draw

explanation.surface: A slow pupil looks for a way to learn drawing.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as an instruction, BACK WARD: WARD backwards makes 'draw'.
explanation.definitionFit: A slow learner, behind in development, was once described as a backward child.

clue.text: Derelict area of Australia about to catch fire earlier in wind

indicators.note: the fire and Australia pieces go inside the wind word

parts.note: to twine is to wind

indicators.note: the fire piece comes before the Australia piece

parts.note: to light is to catch fire

indicators.note: turned about, the Australia letters are read backwards

parts.note: Oz is the informal name for Australia

explanation.surface: A rundown patch of Australian bush about to go up in flames in the wind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' reverses the Australia piece to ZO, and 'earlier' places the fire word ahead of it; 'wind' is the verb, as in coiling, not the breeze.
explanation.definitionFit: A twilight zone is a neglected urban district in decline, or more broadly an ill-defined borderland.

clue.text: Food's offered to work team for a small retainer

parts.note: grub is slang for food, with the 's giving the S
a crew is a team of workers

explanation.surface: Food is laid on for the workers in exchange for a small fee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retainer' is not a fee but something that holds things in place.
explanation.definitionFit: A grub screw is a small headless screw used to hold a part in position on a shaft.

clue.text: Head of house has urge to drink port

indicators.note: the urge word swallows the port

parts.note: to press is to urge
Rio de Janeiro is a Brazilian port

explanation.surface: The head of a household is pressed to have some port.
explanation.walkthrough: 'port' looks like the wine but is a harbour city; 'house' is a religious house.
explanation.definitionFit: A nun in charge of a priory, a religious house, is its superior.

clue.text: Huckster made counterfeit old coin

indicators.note: a counterfeit is a fake version, so these letters are rearranged into a false form

parts.note: taken as written, as part of the letters to shuffle

explanation.surface: A dodgy trader produced fake old currency.
explanation.walkthrough: 'counterfeit' signals rearranging HUCKSTER and MADE together.
explanation.definitionFit: The currency of West Germany and then unified Germany before the euro replaced it in 2002.

clue.text: Area of vessel that's put out of action — about when?

indicators.note: the sunk word goes around the date piece

parts.note: a scuttled ship is sunk and out of action
Dec, December, answers the question when

explanation.surface: Which part of a disabled ship, and when did it happen?
explanation.walkthrough: 'when?' is answered by a month, here December abbreviated; the question mark flags that a date stands in for the question.
explanation.definitionFit: An open upper deck where passengers sit out in the sunshine on a ship.

clue.text: Boastful talk that's on the rise

definitions.meaning: heated gas climbs because it is lighter than cold

explanation.walkthrough: The second reading is literal: warm atmosphere rises.
explanation.definitionFit: Empty, exaggerated or bragging speech is idiomatically called this.

clue.text: Laugh at an evil deed, say, that may be afoot

indicators.note: say signals the letters as heard, not as spelt

parts.note: to laugh at is to mock, then a, then a sin is an evil deed

explanation.surface: Mocking a wicked act, for example.
explanation.walkthrough: MOCK A SIN, spoken, gives the shoe; 'afoot' is literal: worn on the foot.
explanation.definitionFit: A soft leather slip-on shoe is footwear, so it is literally something on a foot.

clue.text: Old judge needs a long time, after flipping rude remark

indicators.note: the long time piece comes after the remark piece
flipped over, the remark word reads backwards

parts.note: a dig is a cutting remark
an eon is an age

explanation.surface: A judge needs ages to recover after a flipping rude comment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flipping' looks like a mild British swear word but turns DIG to GID. Gideon is a judge of Israel in the Old Testament.
explanation.definitionFit: A leader of Israel in the biblical Book of Judges, so an ancient judge.

clue.text: Right round? It could be!

indicators.note: round signals the letters of the word are turned about and rearranged

explanation.surface: Is this the right measure of roundness? It might be!
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' rearranges RIGHT; the whole clue also defines it, since the measurement round something is its girth.
explanation.definitionFit: The measurement around the middle of an object or body is its circumference.

clue.text: City in the south -—- the north has a jetty

parts.note: N is the abbreviation for north
a pier is a jetty

explanation.surface: Contrasting a southern city with the north and its jetty.
explanation.walkthrough: Napier is a city in New Zealand, in the southern hemisphere.
explanation.definitionFit: A port city in Hawke's Bay, New Zealand, in the southern hemisphere.

clue.text: It is no common black tea

parts.words: It is no common black tea
parts.note: a nobleman is no commoner, and the tea named after a peer is a black tea flavoured with bergamot

clue.text: Revise hastily? Will it stick?

clue.text: She served a high flier

explanation.definitionFit: A Wren served in the women's naval service, and the tiny songbird is also a flier.

clue.text: Schoolboy's drunk whisky with meat
